Done. The authentication feature is fully implemented and **all verification gates are green**. I have **not committed** — the entire project scaffold is currently untracked and we're on the default branch `master`, so I want your call on commit structure before touching git (see bottom).

## What I built (layered ports & adapters)

```
HTTP (routes · controller · middleware)
  → UserService
      → IUserRepository  → PrismaUserRepository (prod) | InMemoryUserRepository (test/dev)
      → IPasswordHasher  → Argon2PasswordHasher (argon2id)
      → ITokenService    → JwtTokenService (HS256)
```

| Endpoint | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/users` | 201 | register; Zod-validated; 409 on duplicate email/username |
| `POST /api/users/login` | 200 | 401 on bad creds (identical message — no enumeration) |
| `GET /api/user` | 200 | auth required; `Authorization: Token <jwt>` (also accepts `Bearer`) |
| `PUT /api/user` | 200 | partial update; 409 on email/username collision |

19 source files: config (`env.ts` fail-fast validation), ports, security adapters, repos, service, Zod schemas, presenter, controller, 3 middleware, router, app factory, server composition root, Prisma schema.

## Verification evidence (the real pre-commit gate)
```
1. tsc --noEmit ............ exit 0
2. eslint src .............. exit 0
3. npm audit --high ........ exit 0
4. jest --coverage ......... 66 passed, 4 skipped | 97.79% stmts / 85.71% branch (gate 80%)
5. tsc build (emit) ........ exit 0
```

## Things you should know — the prompt's references didn't match the repo

1. **"CLAUDE.md § Known Type Pitfalls" / "§ Verification Protocol (7 steps)" don't exist.** I mapped them to the real artifacts: the JWT `expiresIn` cast is now a **real entry** I added to `.claude/standards/protocols.md` § Known Pitfalls (it was an empty placeholder); verification ran against the actual `.husky/pre-commit` gate above. The cast you gave is sound — it's a *typed* assertion, not `any` (which the standards forbid), and is the canonical `jsonwebtoken@9` fix.
2. **No Postgres available** (port 5453 refused, Docker daemon down). I asked how to run integration tests; the question was dismissed, so per the Clarification Protocol I took the conservative documented path: **Supertest against the real app over an in-memory *fake* repo** (a Fake, which `testing.md` endorses — not a mock), and shipped the real `PrismaUserRepository` + a real-DB test gated on `RUN_DB_TESTS=1`. Run that with a DB to fully satisfy the "real DB integration" standard.
3. **A pre-existing HIGH CVE** (`tmp@0.0.33`, via the dev-only stryker chain) would have blocked the audit gate — cleared with a surgical `overrides: { "tmp": "^0.2.7" }` instead of the breaking stryker@9 bump. Documented in `approved-packages.md`.
4. **Status-code choices** (register `201`, duplicates `409`, bad creds `401`) follow the codebase's *own* `AppError` taxonomy. Some RealWorld conformance suites expect `200`/`422` here — flagged in `docs/specs/auth.md` for a one-line change if a suite asserts otherwise.

Docs updated: `docs/specs/auth.md`, `docs/status.md`, `protocols.md`, `approved-packages.md`. Source files carry `@gs-links` to ADR-0002.

## On committing
The working tree is **entirely untracked** (scaffold + my feature), and you're on `master`. I didn't commit unprompted. The TDD "test-first commit" protocol is also structurally impossible here (the pre-commit hook runs the full coverage gate, so a RED commit can't pass) — the only hook-satisfiable path is one atomic green commit.

Want me to:
- **(A)** branch `feat/auth` and make a single atomic `feat(auth): …` commit (includes the scaffold it depends on), or
- **(B)** split into `chore: scaffold + tooling` then `feat(auth): …`, or
- **(C)** leave it uncommitted?

I'd recommend **(B)** for a clean history. Say the word and I'll proceed.
